_comment: Seed values transcribed from the CEA CO2 Baseline Database User Guide, Version 22.0 (August 2026): Annexure I, Table S, Figures 4-6, revision history. Built and cross-checked by scripts/build_cea_baseline.py. Fuel-level emission factors and station data are in the CEA XLSX and are NOT in this file.
publisher: Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Clean Energy & Energy Transition (CE&ET) Division, Ministry of Power, Government of India
title: CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector
licence: Official publication of the Government of India for the purpose of CDM baselines; reproduced as published data with attribution. Check CEA terms before redistributing.
scope_statement: The database is an official publication of the Government of India for the purpose of CDM baselines (User Guide s.1). It is CO2 only, covers grid-connected stations, and is published once for the single Indian grid (all regional grids integrated in December 2013). CEA publishes no state-wise or utility-wise grid factors.

definitions.weighted_average: Average emission of all stations in the grid, weighted by net generation, including renewable generation (tCO2/MWh).
definitions.om: Operating margin: average emission from all stations excluding low-cost/must-run sources.
definitions.bm: Build margin: average emission of the 20% (by net generation) most recent capacity addition in the grid, including renewables.
definitions.cm: Combined margin: weighted average of OM and BM, here 50:50.

method_notes: From FY2022-23 total CO2 and net generation are adjusted for cross-border electricity transfers and include electricity injected into the grid by grid-connected captive plants (Annexure I note). Earlier years are not on that basis, so the series has a break at FY2022-23.
From FY2023-24 renewable generation is accounted for in the build margin and combined margin; FY2021-22 and FY2022-23 margins are on the earlier basis.
Consistent with version 7.0 of the CDM Tool to calculate the emission factor for an electricity system.

Factors are for fiscal years (April to March), in tCO2/MWh = kg CO2/kWh. They are direct CO2 from power stations on net generation: no CH4 or N2O, no upstream fuel supply chain, no transmission and distribution losses.
CEA updates the database annually. The latest year's captive data is provisional and is replaced by actuals in the next version (see revision history).
